name: Jotham
bio: Jotham, son of Azariah (Uzziah), governed Judah as regent while his father lived apart as a leper, then succeeded him as king at twenty-five, reigning sixteen years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok. He did right in the LORD's eyes, following his father's example, though the high places remained, and he built the upper gate of the temple (2 Kings 15:5, 32-35) — Chronicles adds that, unlike his father, Jotham never entered the temple itself to do what was not his to do, and that he also rebuilt much of the wall at Ophel, built towns in Judah's hill country and forts and towers in its forests, and defeated the Ammonites, who paid him heavy tribute in silver, wheat, and barley for three years. He grew powerful, Chronicles says, because he walked steadfastly before the LORD his God (2 Chronicles 27:1-6). In his days the LORD began to send Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah against Judah (2 Kings 15:37). He died and was buried in the City of David, and his son Ahaz succeeded him (2 Kings 15:38).
